sections.title: Nature and marks of the Church

questions.prompt: What must be present for a community to be recognized as a Christian church?
questions.displayNote: Foundational  |  On entry to this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: A people gathered in the name of Jesus Christ and confessing the apostolic faith.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Faithful proclamation of the gospel.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Baptism and the Lord’s Supper celebrated as Christ instituted them.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Recognized ministry in continuity with the apostles.

choices.label: E
choices.text: A community accountable for discipleship and discipline.

choices.label: F
choices.text: Visible communion with the wider church.

choices.label: G
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: Can a congregation be gravely defective in doctrine or practice and still be a church?
questions.displayNote: Common follow-up  |  All readers of this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes, while the gospel and what constitutes a church remain present.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Its standing depends on its continuing communion with the body authorized to recognize it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Christ alone knows its standing. Other Christians can judge particular errors without deciding whether it is a church.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: Two congregations proclaim Christ faithfully but refuse communion with each other. What does their division show?
questions.displayNote: Common follow-up  |  All readers of this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: They can both be churches while bearing a real wound to Christian unity.

choices.label: B
choices.text: At least one lacks full visible communion with the church in a way that matters for its ecclesial standing.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Their separation may be faithful if communion would require denial of essential truth.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I would need to know why fellowship was broken before judging its significance.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

introduction: In these questions a local congregation, a wider communion, and the whole people of God are named separately where the distinction matters.
editorialNotes: Ask what makes a community a church before asking how faithfully it lives out its calling. Reuse SAC-23 on the administration of the sacraments.

furtherStudy.text: Vatican II, Lumen gentium, §§8 and 14–16, on the visible church and communion.

sections.title: Visible and invisible Church

questions.prompt: How do those visibly associated with the church relate to those who truly belong to Christ?
questions.displayNote: Foundational  |  On entry to this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: The visible community includes some without saving faith. The church known perfectly to God consists of those truly united to Christ.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Christ founded one visible communion. People can belong to it outwardly in different degrees or fail to live by its grace.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A local church should ordinarily consist of professing believers, though the sincerity of professions is known fully to God.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I affirm a spiritual fellowship in Christ without identifying it with one visible body or boundary.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: Can people outside the visible boundaries of your own communion belong to Christ’s church?
questions.displayNote: ↳ After ECC-04, if B or D is selected.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes, as members of other churches in the full sense.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes, through a real but imperfect communion with Christ’s church.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They may belong to Christ in ways known to God, while the church’s visible boundaries remain definite.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I identify belonging to Christ’s church with membership in the visible communion.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

editorialNotes: “Visible” and “invisible” can describe aspects of one church or express a distinction some traditions reject.

sections.title: Church government and polity

questions.prompt: A congregation disputes the removal of its pastor. Who has authority to make a binding ecclesial decision?
questions.displayNote: Foundational  |  On entry to this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: The local congregation has final authority.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The congregation’s elders have final local authority.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A council or assembly of elders beyond the congregation can give a binding judgment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A bishop or other episcopal authority has jurisdiction.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Authority is shared, with different bodies able to authorize, review, or confirm the decision.

choices.label: F
choices.text: My tradition seeks corporate discernment and would frame this in terms of unity rather than final jurisdiction.

choices.label: G
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: Can a general council issue a doctrinal decision that binds local churches?
questions.displayNote: Common follow-up  |  All readers of this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes, under the conditions that give a council authority over the whole church.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes, for churches accountable to that council, subject to correction by Scripture.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Its determinations carry weight but bind a congregation only through that congregation’s own reception.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A council may testify to truth but has no power to bind consciences by its own decision.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

editorialNotes: Do not infer the final seat of authority from the presence of bishops, elders, or congregational votes alone.

furtherStudy.text: Baptist Faith and Message, article VI, on the local church and its offices.

sections.title: Ordination and ministerial offices

questions.displayNote: Foundational  |  On entry to this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: Through prayer and laying on of hands, God confers a sacramental gift for ordained ministry.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It authorizes someone to exercise a recognized ministry of word, sacrament, or oversight.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It publicly recognizes a calling and gifts God has already given.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I do not recognize a distinct ordained ministry.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: Which best describes oversight in your church’s understanding of ministry?
questions.displayNote: Common follow-up  |  All readers of this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bishops, presbyters or priests, and deacons constitute distinct orders.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bishop and elder name the same governing or pastoral office, distinct from deacon.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pastor or elder and deacon are local roles whose organization a congregation determines.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Spirit may raise ministries without establishing a permanent set of offices.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I recognize a different structure, such as an ongoing fivefold ministry of apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors, and teachers.

choices.label: F
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: May someone with evident pastoral gifts exercise public oversight before receiving formal recognition?
questions.displayNote: Common follow-up  |  All readers of this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gifts alone do not authorize public oversight. Recognition by the proper ecclesial body is necessary.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A congregation’s call can authorize oversight before a formal ordination service.

choices.label: C
choices.text: In exceptional circumstances the church can receive ministry later recognized as a genuine call.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I do not distinguish a formal office of oversight from a ministry the community discerns as it occurs.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

editorialNotes: Distinguish ordination’s effect from the list of offices a tradition recognizes.

sections.title: Gender and church leadership

questions.prompt: Which ministries, if recognized in your tradition, may women exercise on the same terms as men?
questions.displayNote: Foundational  |  On entry to this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: Serve as deacons.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Preach to the gathered congregation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Teach adult men and women in settings outside gathered worship.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Serve as elders, presbyters, or priests.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serve as senior pastors or bishops with final pastoral oversight.

choices.label: F
choices.text: I would reserve all the listed ministries to men.

choices.label: G
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: If a church reserves an office to men, does that also reserve particular acts of teaching to men?
questions.displayNote: ↳ After ECC-10, if A or B or C or D is selected.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes, the restriction concerns the act of authoritative teaching as well as the office.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A woman may teach or preach under the responsible oversight of those who hold the office.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The office itself is reserved, but women may exercise the same acts of teaching without a special requirement of male oversight.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I do not reserve an office to men.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

editorialNotes: Office, ordination, and acts of teaching can have different boundaries. Do not assume titles mean the same thing in every polity.

furtherStudy.text: Assemblies of God, “Women in Ministerial Leadership,” on eligibility for ministry.

sections.title: Apostolic succession

questions.prompt: What makes a church’s ministry apostolic?
questions.displayNote: Foundational  |  On entry to this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: Faithfulness to the apostles’ teaching.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Continuity in the apostolic mission of witness and service.

choices.label: C
choices.text: An unbroken succession of episcopal ordinations.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Recognition and communion among churches that continue the apostles’ ministry.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: Suppose a community preserves apostolic teaching but lacks demonstrable episcopal succession. How would you judge its ministry?
questions.displayNote: Common follow-up  |  All readers of this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: Its ministers can be fully authorized by a faithful church.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It can have real Christian ministry while lacking something required for the fullness of ordained ministry.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Apostolic teaching alone cannot supply valid sacramental ordination.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I would suspend judgment about historical succession rather than infer either validity or invalidity.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

introduction: Episcopal succession is a succession of bishops in ordained ministry.
editorialNotes: Distinguish succession in teaching, succession in office, and sacramental recognition.

furtherStudy.text: World Council of Churches, Baptism, Eucharist and Ministry, “Ministry,” §§34–38, on succession in the apostolic tradition.

sections.title: Church discipline

questions.prompt: What can exclusion from church fellowship establish about a person’s standing before God?
questions.displayNote: Foundational  |  On entry to this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is a serious church judgment about a public profession. God alone knows the heart.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A duly authorized judgment has spiritual effect in the church’s exercise of the keys, while remaining ordered toward restoration.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It sets a boundary for communal life without issuing a judgment about salvation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: My tradition does not practice formal exclusion.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: A disciplined leader repents and returns to fellowship. Can the original misconduct permanently disqualify that person from office?
questions.displayNote: Common follow-up  |  All readers of this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes. Some misconduct permanently disqualifies a person from certain offices.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Permanent disqualification is possible, but only after a judgment about enduring qualifications or trust in the particular case.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No. The church may require time and evidence of fitness, but past misconduct cannot by itself create permanent ineligibility.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I do not recognize a distinct office that requires reinstatement.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: What should restoration to fellowship ordinarily require from a person under discipline?
questions.displayNote: Common follow-up  |  All readers of this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: A credible profession of repentance.

choices.label: B
choices.text: An end to the conduct for which the person was disciplined.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reasonable efforts to make amends where possible.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A formal act of reconciliation or absolution by the responsible church authority.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

editorialNotes: Distinguish removal from fellowship, restrictions on particular ministries, and restoration to communion.

Enter at any dimension. In guided mode, begin with its opening question, continue through the main questions in the order shown, and insert a follow-up only when its stated answer matches. After the branch, resume with the next main question. A skipped answer or uncertainty opens no conditional branch unless specified.

Choose the closest single answer unless multiple selections are invited. On multiple-response questions, an uncertainty or “none” choice stands alone. Treat unresolved tensions as invitations to clarify.

vocabulary.definition: The study of what the Church is, how it is ordered, and what it is called to do.
Qualities by which Christians identify the Church or assess how faithfully a particular church lives.
The Church as an identifiable community in history, with public confession, worship, and membership.
The Church considered as all who truly belong to Christ, whose full membership is known to God.
The way a church organizes leadership, decision-making, and authority.
A church’s formal act of setting someone apart for a recognized ministry or office.
Continuity of the Church’s ministry with the apostles, understood in terms of handed-down teaching, succession in office, or both.
Continuity in the office of bishop through an identifiable succession of bishops.
A church’s formal response to serious wrongdoing or doctrinal error for the sake of correction, restoration, or the community’s care.
